solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Monk's Fiat on hill

parts.note: a ben is a Scottish mountain or hill, as in Ben Nevis
a fiat is an official decree

explanation.surface: A monk's little Italian car parked up on a hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiat' looks like the car maker, but it is the common noun meaning an authoritative order; 'on' puts the hill first.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Benedict was the sixth-century monk who founded Western monasticism and wrote its famous Rule.

clue.text: Big bird carries black dog

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for black, as on pencils
an eagle is a large bird of prey

explanation.surface: A huge bird of prey flies off clutching a black dog.
explanation.walkthrough: The short abbreviation is carried at the head of the bird in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The beagle is a small scent hound breed, originally kept for hunting hares.

clue.text: A heavyweight upset railway official

indicators.note: in a down entry, something upset is turned upside down, so the letters run from bottom to top

parts.note: A plus a ton, a very heavy weight
RY is a standard abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A burly boxer has upset a railway employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A heavyweight' suggests a boxer, but it is A plus a unit of weight; 'railway official' looks like one phrase but splits between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A notary is a public official authorised to witness documents and certify deeds.

clue.text: Interpreters start to discuss part of New Testament about silver

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of discuss

indicators.note: about here means placed around, so the book's name wraps the metal

parts.note: the Epistle to the Romans is a book of the New Testament
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Translators begin a discussion of a scriptural book concerning silver, perhaps Judas's thirty pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: The metal sits inside the epistle's name, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragoman was an interpreter or guide in Arabic-, Turkish- or Persian-speaking countries.

clue.text: See nervous merchant when speaking on revolutionary fast food

indicators.note: nervous suggests jittery and agitated, so the letters jump into a new order

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine-born Marxist revolutionary
the three letters of see rearranged

indicators.note: when speaking means the word is judged by how it is said out loud, not spelt

parts.note: a burgher is a town citizen, typically a merchant or trader

explanation.surface: An instruction to watch a jittery trader talking about a fast-food revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: In this down entry 'on' puts the revolutionary on top of the rest; burgher and the bun-based snack sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheeseburger is a hamburger topped with a slice of cheese, a staple of takeaway menus.

clue.text: Short deer, goat and badger

indicators.note: something cut short loses its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a hart is a male red deer
goat is slang for a foolish person, as is ass

explanation.surface: A list of three animals: a small deer, a goat and a badger.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a menagerie, and 'badger' looks like the third animal, but it is the verb meaning to pester; goat and ass are both words for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: To badger someone is to pester them persistently, which is to harass them.

clue.text: Got up with a bourbon, say

parts.note: taken as written
the Bourbon rose is a variety of rose, so it is an example of one

explanation.surface: Someone got out of bed and reached for a whiskey.
explanation.walkthrough: Bourbon suggests American whiskey, but here it is the old garden rose group named after the Île Bourbon; 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Arose is the past tense of arise, meaning stood up or got out of bed.

clue.text: Attempt to hold a doctor following a very old scientist

indicators.note: to hold something is to have it within your grip, so one piece goes inside another
following means coming after, so the attempt with its contents is placed second, behind the opening words

parts.note: taken as written
V is the standard abbreviation for very
O is a standard abbreviation for old
to have a go is to make an attempt
taken as written
Dr is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: An elderly scientist trying to restrain a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: The attempt wraps the second A and the doctor, and the whole comes after 'a very old', which reads naturally as describing the scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: Amedeo Avogadro was the Italian scientist behind Avogadro's law and the constant named after him.

clue.text: South London district in Bexley is an area suffering inflation

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for south
Welling is a district of south-east London in the borough of Bexley

explanation.surface: A south London neighbourhood is suffering from rising prices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inflation' points to economics, but the definition means a part of the body puffing up; Bexley is a London borough.
explanation.definitionFit: A swelling is a place on the body that has become enlarged or puffed up, so literally inflated.

clue.text: Might one entertain soldiers for dinner?

definitions.text: Might one entertain soldiers for dinner?

parts.words: Might one entertain soldiers for dinner?
parts.note: surface reading: a host who throws dinner parties for troops
setter's reading: soldiers are soldier ants, and dinner is what they become for a creature that eats insects

explanation.walkthrough: 'Entertain soldiers for dinner' sounds like hospitality, but the soldiers are ants and they are the meal, not the guests.
explanation.definitionFit: An anteater is a long-snouted mammal that feeds on ants and termites, soldier castes included.

clue.text: Second pink wine is sour

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second, as in 'wait a mo'
rosé is pink wine

explanation.surface: A glass of rosé tastes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sour' looks like a verdict on the wine, but it describes a mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Morose means gloomy and sullen, the same bad temper as being sour.

clue.text: Halt donation that's corrupt with utmost force

indicators.note: something corrupt has been spoiled and altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A call to stop a gift that is tainted, fought with all possible force.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a charity scandal; the first two words are the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To fight tooth and nail is an idiom meaning to struggle fiercely with every means available.

clue.text: Musical composition left on fabulous ship

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
the Argo was the ship of Jason and the Argonauts in Greek myth

explanation.surface: A piece of music abandoned aboard a legendary ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' here means belonging to fable or legend, not wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: A largo is a piece or movement played in a slow, broad tempo, such as Handel's famous Largo.

clue.text: Obstruct modern portico being built across two lakes

indicators.note: something built across a space spans it, so the portico straddles the word for modern

parts.note: a stoa is a classical covered colonnade or portico
modern means new
L is the abbreviation for lake, twice

explanation.surface: A modern colonnade is being built across two lakes, blocking the view.
explanation.walkthrough: The Greek portico wraps the word for modern, then the two lakes follow.
explanation.definitionFit: To stonewall is to block or delay by refusing to answer or cooperate, an idiom from cricket.

clue.text: Using gas with caution — about to enter underground tunnels

parts.note: to gas or rabbit on is to chatter at length

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: to caution someone is to warn them
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A warning about using poison gas in subterranean tunnels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gas' suggests poison gas in tunnels, but it is the informal verb for chattering; 'rabbit' means the same in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbit warren is a network of interconnecting burrows dug by rabbits beneath the ground.

clue.text: A group of preservationists take lorry around cold area to the south

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the lorry wraps the letter for cold

parts.note: taken as written
the National Trust is a British conservation body that preserves historic places
an artic is an articulated lorry
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Conservationists drive a truck around a frozen southern region.
explanation.walkthrough: The NT, or National Trust, looks after Britain's historic houses and countryside; an artic is the British short name for an articulated lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Antarctic is the polar region around the South Pole, the coldest part of the globe.

clue.text: Green light gets bus ruined in crash

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the word is broken up and its letters rearranged
in means placed inside, so the jumbled letters go within the word for crash

parts.note: a thump is a heavy blow or crash
the three letters of bus rearranged

explanation.surface: Traffic lights turn green and a bus is wrecked in a collision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green light' reads as a traffic signal, but it means approval.
explanation.definitionFit: A thumbs-up is a sign of approval, just as a green light is permission to go ahead.

clue.text: Get container for rubbish and clean new housing for sailors?

indicators.note: new suggests remade into a fresh form, so the letters take a different order

parts.note: a bin is a receptacle for rubbish
the five letters of clean rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions to fetch a rubbish bin and clean up new quarters for the crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Housing for sailors' suggests living quarters; the question mark warns it houses something sailors use, the compass.
explanation.definitionFit: A binnacle is the stand on a ship's deck that houses the compass, so it is a housing used by seafarers.

clue.text: Top managers head off to centre of Heathrow to collect food — it isn't far…

indicators.note: to collect something is to gather it in, so one piece goes around another
with the head taken off, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: chairs are the people who head boards and committees
bread is a staple food

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle, so only the middle letters are kept

parts.note: the two middle letters of the eight-letter Heathrow

explanation.surface: Executives head to Heathrow for a bite to eat, since the airport isn't far away.
explanation.walkthrough: The beheaded executives and the airport's centre together wrap the food. The ellipsis carries the clue on into the next one.
explanation.definitionFit: A hair's breadth is a tiny distance or margin, so something at that distance is very close.

clue.text: Meet at Queen's Snug?

parts.note: lines that meet join
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: An invitation to meet in the snug, the cosy back bar, of the Queen's pub.
explanation.walkthrough: A snug is a small private room in a British pub, but here Snug is the joiner among Shakespeare's mechanicals in A Midsummer Night's Dream; the question mark flags the example.
explanation.definitionFit: Snug is the joiner who plays the Lion in A Midsummer Night's Dream, so he is an example of a carpenter.

clue.text: Hostel has awful butter

indicators.note: awful means dreadful and in a mess, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the three letters of has rearranged
a ram butts with its horns, so it is literally a butter

explanation.surface: A youth hostel serves terrible butter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butter' looks like the dairy spread, but it is one who butts.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashram is a religious retreat or hermitage in India where people stay and lodge, loosely a hostel.

clue.text: … and head away from Somerset resort to handle a situation beset with problems

parts.note: taken as written: the word to be removed

indicators.note: with the named word sent away, it is removed from the resort's name

parts.note: Minehead is a seaside resort town on the Somerset coast in south-west England
to field a question is to handle it

explanation.surface: Following on from the previous clue, a manager leaves a seaside resort to deal with a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: Minehead is a holiday town on the Bristol Channel; take away the word head and the first half is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A minefield is figuratively a situation full of hidden dangers or difficulties.

clue.text: Many ships moving rapidly

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a group of vessels sailing together

explanation.surface: A flotilla sweeping across the sea at speed.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names a navy's body of vessels; the adjective is a literary word for swift and nimble.

clue.text: Gives support to Australians about test opener

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the Australians wrap the letter

parts.note: roos, short for kangaroos, is a nickname for Australians, notably the rugby league team

indicators.note: an opener comes first, so only the first letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of test

explanation.surface: Cricket fans cheer on Australia as the Test match opens.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a cricket Test between nations; the definition is the verb in 'roots for', to cheer on.
explanation.definitionFit: To root for a team is to cheer and back it, so roots means gives support.

clue.text: Private note hidden in camp

indicators.note: something tucked inside sits within another word, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: a camp is a faction or group sharing views, like a sect
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A soldier's private letter concealed in an army camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' and 'camp' suggest the army, but private is an adjective meaning confidential.
explanation.definitionFit: Something secret is kept private, known only to a few people.

clue.text: Safer net transported catch

indicators.note: things transported are moved about, so the letters shift into a new order

parts.note: taken as written: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A more secure net was used to carry the fish caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catch' suggests a haul of fish alongside the net, but it is the noun for a clasp or latch.
explanation.definitionFit: A catch is a device that fastens a door, window or bag, so a type of fastener.

clue.text: Moderately attractive

definitions.meaning: second meaning: pleasing to look at

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one phrase grading someone's looks, but each word is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb the word means fairly or quite; as an adjective it means good-looking in a delicate way.

clue.text: Pick large crumpet looking fresh on the outside

indicators.note: to look fresh is to appear renewed, so the word is remade in a different order
on the outside means wrapping round, so the remade word encloses the other piece

parts.note: the seven letters of crumpet rearranged
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Choosing the big crumpet that looks freshest at the bakery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pick' seems to mean choose a crumpet, but it is the noun for what a guitarist strums with.
explanation.definitionFit: A plectrum is a small flat piece used to pluck guitar strings, commonly called a pick.
